themes.title: Weightlessness and letting go
themes.body: Stories about dreams often connect falling with a moment that feels outside our control. It may also echo the weightless sensation of the body relaxing as sleep begins. It does not predict something bad.
themes.prompt: Is there anything you would like to set down for a while?

themes.title: Chasing and avoiding
themes.body: Being chased is often described as an imaginative rehearsal of pressure or unfinished concerns. It may simply be a vivid story that was easier to remember.
themes.prompt: If you could pause inside the dream, what help would you want first?

themes.title: Change and self-consciousness
themes.body: Dreams about teeth are common. People sometimes connect them with change, appearance, or expression; they can also reflect sensations from the mouth during sleep.
themes.prompt: Is there a small change in life that still feels unfamiliar?

themes.title: Water and moving feelings
themes.body: Water in dreams is often used as a metaphor for emotion: still water can feel calm, while rough water can feel like too much information. The personal meaning belongs to the dreamer.
themes.prompt: Did the water make you want to approach, move away, or simply watch?

themes.title: Freedom and perspective
themes.body: Flying dreams are often playfully linked with freedom, curiosity, or seeing things from farther away. Fear in the dream may instead reflect the imagined loss of solid ground.
themes.prompt: While flying, did you feel more like exploring or looking for somewhere to land?

themes.title: School and being evaluated
themes.body: School and exam dreams are common even years after graduation. They are often read as a collage of feeling unprepared, being evaluated, and old memories.
themes.prompt: Has anything recently made you feel as though you are being graded?

themes.title: Finding direction
themes.body: Getting lost or missing transport in a dream is often connected with pace, choices, or fear of running late. The brain may also be rearranging familiar places.
themes.prompt: Without any need to hurry, which turning point would you want to see more clearly?

themes.title: Instinct and companionship
themes.body: Animals carry very different meanings across cultures. Your own feeling of familiarity, fear, or closeness in the dream may be more interesting than a fixed symbol.
themes.prompt: Did the animal feel like a companion, a signal, or an unfamiliar visitor?

themes.title: Space and inner rooms
themes.body: Houses in dreams are often treated as metaphors for the self and one's living space. A new room may suggest novelty, or simply a rearranged memory of real places.
themes.prompt: Which part of that space made you want to stay a little longer?

themes.title: Energy and change
themes.body: In stories, fire can mean destruction, warmth, or renewal. The feeling inside your dream is more interesting than any fixed prediction of good or bad luck.
themes.prompt: Did the fire feel dangerous, warm, or connected with something you wanted to change?

fallback.title: A collage that belongs to you
fallback.body: Dreams combine memories, sensations, and chance fragments, so there may be no standard answer. The feeling that remains after waking can be the most interesting clue.
fallback.prompt: What stays with you most: an image, a person, or a feeling?
